cards.explanation: The answer is to call out to Him. God tells Jeremiah, "Call to Me, and I will answer and show you great and unsearchable things you do not know." (Jeremiah 33:3) Jeremiah is still confined, and the offer stands anyway. I sat at the back of a junk drawer for years, friends, and a line like that would have made my whole week.

The answer is False. God promises "…great and unsearchable things you do not know." (Jeremiah 33:3) Not review, not a reminder, brand new things. A teacher who only repeats what you already know is just an echo, and God is no echo.

The answer is because of all its wickedness. God says, "I have hidden My face from this city because of all its wickedness." (Jeremiah 33:5) The text gives the reason right there, so we don't have to guess. It's a heavy line, friends, and I think it's meant to be taken seriously.

The answer is health and healing. God says, "…I will bring to it health and healing, and I will heal its people…" (Jeremiah 33:6) Anger and a hidden face in one verse, then healing in the next. I'd happily trade a hundred burnt batches for that kind of turnaround.

The answer is True. God says, "I will restore Judah and Israel from captivity and will rebuild them as in former times." (Jeremiah 33:7) That's a big promise to make when the Chaldeans are coming to fight. It lands even harder when you know Jeremiah is confined in the courtyard of the guard.

The answer is forgive. Here God speaks: "And I will cleanse them from all the iniquity they have committed against Me, and will forgive all their sins of rebellion against Me." (Jeremiah 33:8) He promises both cleansing and forgiveness in the same breath, friends. That kind of mercy is worth way more than a whole batch of fresh cookies.

The answer is that they tremble in awe. God says the nations "…will tremble in awe because of all the goodness and prosperity that I will provide for it." (Jeremiah 33:9) They hear about the good God does, and it stops them in their tracks. I think that's the kind of news you repeat to everyone you meet.

The answer is sounds of joy and gladness! God says there "will be heard again the sounds of joy and gladness…" (Jeremiah 33:10-11) Streets that were deserted get loud again, in the best way. I'm a big fan of noise like that.

The answer is a bride and bridegroom. God lists "…the voices of the bride and bridegroom…" among the joyful sounds. (Jeremiah 33:11) A wedding is one of the happiest sounds a street can have. Streets that once sat empty will hear that again.

The answer is True. God says the sounds will include "…the voices of those bringing thank offerings into the house of the LORD…" (Jeremiah 33:11) People will walk in with thanks again, friends. And what they say is simple and good: "Give thanks to the LORD of Hosts, for the LORD is good…"

The answer is pastures. God says, "…there will once more be pastures for shepherds to rest their flocks." (Jeremiah 33:12) A place without people or animals gets shepherds and sheep again. It would be a nice spot for a rest.

The answer is False! The flocks will pass under the hands of the one who counts them in the hill country, the foothills, the Negev, Benjamin's land, the cities around Jerusalem and the cities of Judah. (Jeremiah 33:13) God's promise reaches way beyond one city. Whoever does the counting is going to be busy.

The answer is True, friends. God says of the Branch, "…He will administer justice and righteousness in the land." (Jeremiah 33:15) God is the One who causes this Branch to sprout for David, so the Branch's work is justice and righteousness. Sprouting is such a gentle word for something so big.

The answer is The LORD Our Righteousness! God says, "…this is the name by which it will be called: The LORD Our Righteousness." (Jeremiah 33:16) It comes right after Judah is saved and Jerusalem dwells securely. That's a name worth living up to.

The answer is False. God says, "David will never lack a man to sit on the throne of the house of Israel…" (Jeremiah 33:17) Never lack means there will always be a man for it. That's a promise with no expiration date.

The answer is offering sacrifices. God says the priests who are Levites will always have a man before Him "…to offer burnt offerings, to burn grain offerings, and to present sacrifices." (Jeremiah 33:18) Those are the duties He names. Every time I read a list like that I think of my own busy mornings in the bakery.

The answer is the day and the night! God says, "If you can break My covenant with the day and My covenant with the night… then My covenant may also be broken with David My servant." (Jeremiah 33:20-21) And nobody can break the day and night. Every sunrise is a little reminder.

The answer is False. God says His covenant with David and the Levites could be broken only if His covenant with the day and the night could be broken, so that they stopped keeping their appointed time. (Jeremiah 33:20-21) Day and night aren't breaking, friends. That's the whole comparison.

The answer is the sand on the seashore. God says, "As the hosts of heaven cannot be counted and as the sand on the seashore cannot be measured, so too will I multiply the descendants of My servant David and the Levites who minister before Me." (Jeremiah 33:22) The hosts of heaven and the sand on the seashore are the two things He sets beside them. That's a lot of descendants.

The answer is despise. God says, "So they despise My people and no longer regard them as a nation." (Jeremiah 33:24) It comes from what these people are saying: that the LORD has rejected the two families He chose. I think that's a hurtful thing to say about anyone.

The answer is compassion, friends. God closes with this: "For I will restore them from captivity and will have compassion on them." (Jeremiah 33:26) That's how the passage ends. It's a gentle ending, and I like it.
